procedure.step: The Ministry of Economy and Tourism requires the factory to be registered through its Factory Registration service before applying for a certificate of origin for India. Registration requires the factory to be located outside a free zone, a MoIAT industrial licence, and a MoIAT letter confirming 40% domestic value added, and takes about 3 working days.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The Ministry of Foreign Trade issues the preferential certificate of origin for India through its e-service. The applicant must log in to the ministry e-services portal, choose the Certificate of Origin for India service, fill in the application form, upload the required documents (proof of factory registration, the commercial invoice, and, for a trading exporter, the factory's purchase invoice), pay the fee online, and submit the application. Processing takes about one working day, and the service runs 24/7.

The Ministry of Foreign Trade charges a certificate fee of AED 50 for this shipment, as the invoice value falls within the band up to AED 100000, based on the fee schedule in Cabinet Resolution 208/2025.

The competent authority issues the certificate of origin before, at, or within five working days of the date of exportation. The certificate is valid for twelve months from the date of issue and covers only one import, although it may list several products. It may be issued retrospectively up to twelve months from the date of shipment, marked 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' in box 9 of India's certificate form.

The issuing authority requires the application to include the HS code, description, quantity and value of the exported product, and each item must qualify separately in its own right. The authority may ask for detailed cost sheets and conduct a factory visit.

The exporter must ensure the goods are shipped directly from the UAE to India. Transit through another country is allowed only under customs control, with no operations other than unloading, reloading, storage or similar. If a third party issues the invoice, the exporter must indicate 'third-party invoicing'.

The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry and must hold origin information under CAROTAR 2020, including which origin criterion is claimed. The importer keeps supporting documents for at least five years from filing and must answer a customs request within ten working days. Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to e-Sanchit, but this is unconfirmed as it comes from secondary sources.

The exporter must keep origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least five years from the end of the calendar year of the certificate's issue. The exporter must also consent to verification visits; refusal is grounds for denying preferential benefits.

caveats.note: Estimate on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
'+' in a rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.

The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty (BCD), and the Agriculture Infrastructure and Development Cess only for lines in Table II. IGST, GST compensation cess and the Social Welfare Surcharge still apply, as do any anti-dumping, countervailing or safeguard duties. Because the IGST base includes BCD, a lower BCD also lowers the IGST amount.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.

Inference: a producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.

That electronic certificates are accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system comes from CBIC Instruction 28/2022, which Mansha has read only through secondary reports (LiveLaw, taxmann), not the official text.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
